the consistency problem is undecidable for arbitrary constraints, NP-complete for unary keys, and coNP-complete for negated constraints.

the consistency and implication problems are decidable for unary keys and unary foreign keys, but undecidable for general foreign keys, and that the consistency problem is NP-complete for unary keys, but undetermined for unary foreign keys.
the complexity of the problem is NP-complete for unary keys, and coNP-complete for foreign keys.

the fundamental problem of checking the consistency of XML specifications.
the fundamental problem of specifying XML data in a meaningful way.

the fundamental question of whether an integrity constraint is satisfied by an XML document that conforms to a DTD, and with the implication problem of whether a given set of integrity constraints implies another one.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consistency and implication problems are in general undecidable, but that they become decidable in many cases, and that they are NP-complete for unary keys.
the consistency problem for DTDs and constraints is undecidable, while the implication problem is coNP-complete.

the problem of checking consistency and implication for XML integrity constraints is NP-complete, and the problem of checking implication is coNP-complete, in the presence of unary keys and foreignkeys.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of DTLs and unary integrity constraints makes the problem NP-complete, while the addition of negation makes the problem coNP-complete.

the consistency problem and the implication problem are intractable in the presence of negations and that, when negations are absent, the implication problem is coNP-complete while the consistency problem is NP-complete.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of a DTD, the integrity constraints on XML documents are not as simple to reason with as one may expect.

the presence of DDTs makes the problem of reasoning about constraints much harder, and that the complexity of the consistency problem is determined by the interplay between the DTD and the constraints.
